newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farm group asks Congress to solve IRS dispute.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm group asks Congress to solve IRS dispute.

text.p: The American Farm Bureau Federation on Friday said it asked Congress to help solve a dispute with the Internal Revenue Service on when farmers must pay taxes on deferred payment grain contracts.

"The Tax Reform Act of 1986 supports the position that farmers' deferred payment contracts should not be included in any calculation of the Alternative Minimum Tax (AMT)," Farm Bureau President Dean Kleckner said in a letter to Congress.
The IRS said farmers have to report income from deferred payment grain sales under AMT in the year the sale was made instead of the year the farmer received payment.
AMT taxes a broader range of income at a lower rate than normal income tax.
Farmers have long used deferred payment contracts to balance income from year to year.
"Farmers and ranchers across America need Congress to act in advance of their 1996 income tax filing deadline to correct this interpretation," Kleckner said.
Several congressional leaders have said they will support an exemption that protects farmers from having to report income under AMT in the year the sale was made.
